audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was Skill while whys[0] says Mini's autos and a Boomerang win the first trade outright. First item and 2+ items were given to Gnar while whys[5] says the lane equalises around first items and whys[6] says Maokai out-sustains and out-scales.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Maokai/Maokai on a 48.91% win rate — early Gnar, late Maokai. The prose said that; the sides did not.
audit.corrected: Level 1 flipped to Gnar at 6/10; First item flipped to Maokai at 4/10; 2+ items flipped to Maokai at 3/10 with phases[6].why rewritten. Chart now matches the packet on all seven rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the first-item / 2-item swing was attributed vaguely to 'Saplings and passive sustain'.
audit.why: Bramble Smash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5 — the knockback is available almost constantly, which is why standing still is punished rather than merely risky. Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10, and that is the cooldown the whole page claims to track. Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90 at 3000 range.
audit.corrected: Bramble Smash's 5-7s and Twisted Advance's range written into early; the sustain swing re-explained through Sap Magic's actual mechanic in whys[5], spikes[3].text and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields call Maokai immobile — 'immobile Maokai can't punish back without walking forward', 'exactly the immobile, melee-range body my Mini form was built to abuse'. His W's untargetability is absent, and Sap Magic's cooldown-reduction mechanic is absent.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is a 525-range TARGETED dash that roots on arrival and makes him untargetable while it travels. Calling him immobile is the exact opposite of the truth, and it is the one thing that breaks the kiting plan this page is built on: spacing does not prevent a targeted dash, and any Boomerang or Wallop spent into the dash whiffs entirely because he cannot be hit during it. Sap Magic's heal cooldown is reduced every time Maokai casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy spell — so Gnar's own poke accelerates the sustain that undoes it, which is what actually flattens the lane at first items and what makes Executioner's a real purchase rather than boilerplate.
audit.corrected: Immobility claims replaced with the dash-root in whys[2], spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]; untargetability written into mid; Sap Magic's mechanic written into whys[5], spikes[3].text and late.

Throw Q to slow him before he closes, catch it on the return for the cooldown refund, and never give him a stationary Mini target to engage onto.
edits.after: Maokai is the melee-range body your Mini form was built to abuse — stand at Boomerang range, land the third Hyper hit for the move-speed proc, and chip him while his only reach is a Sapling he can't land on a kiting Mini. Two traps. Bramble Smash knocks you back every 5-7 seconds if a squishy Mini body sits still. And Twisted Advance is a 525-range targeted dash-root, so once it is ranked spacing alone will not save you — hold Hop for it. Throw Q to slow him before he closes and catch it on the return for the refund.

notes: Headline error: the page describes Maokai as immobile in five places. Twisted Advance is a targeted 525-range dash that roots on arrival and is untargetable in flight — he is not immobile, spacing does not answer him, and anything you throw into the dash whiffs. Second: Sap Magic's heal cooldown shortens both when he casts and when he is HIT by an enemy spell, so Gnar's poke actively speeds up the healing meant to be undone by it. That is the real reason the lane flattens at first items, and it is what justifies the anti-heal already listed in report[8].t. One string I could not reach: dontsFull[2].t 'Eat his R knockback' is 19 characters, under the applier's 25-char skip threshold — Nature's Grasp roots, it does not knock back. I corrected the same phrase inside report[11].t, which is long enough to apply.
